rationale.text: Each of the 64 rows is independent; mapping row-loop `i` to parallel GPU thread-blocks lets all 30 SMs contribute and eliminates sequential row iteration. With 64 rows and 30 SMs this gives ~2 waves — close to full utilisation.

Tiling the reduction axis `j` with 1024 threads per tile matches the max_threads_per_block=1024 on Ampere. For a 4096-wide row, this creates 4 chunks that can be reduced with efficient warp-shuffle + shared-memory tree reductions. 1024 elements × 4 bytes = 4 KB per tile, well within the 49 KB shared memory budget.

Vectorizing the inner reduction loop `j` with width=4 enables 128-bit memory loads (float4), which is the optimal load width on Ampere for FP32. This improves memory bandwidth utilization for the row-wise read pattern and reduces instruction count by 4×.
